findings.note: All 874 input names were semantically reviewed individually. KJV governs identity/context. Hitchcock remains an attributed historical proposal; this file does not replace Scripture. Corroborated means broad lexical agreement only, never biblical verification or proof of derivation.

Comparison uses the pinned OpenScriptures digital transcription in audit/name-sources/sources.json, not facsimiles of original Strong printings. Errors detected in this snapshot are not thereby proven present in James Strong's original edition. No BDB or modern substitute dictionary was used. No independent Webster1828 entries were consulted in this batch; English paraphrases are editorial explanations, not Webster attestations.
A corroborated status can concern one supported core sense; per-entry notes explicitly reject additional unsupported alternatives. Agreement is semantic, not automatic matching of English words.
Multiple Hebrew forms, people, places, titles or ordinary words share English spellings. Keep the entry-specific distinctions and KJV contexts; do not assign a single meaning to every occurrence.

Non was falsely offered G137 Aenon; Bethuel initially only H1329 Bethul; Ezer only H687 treasure (omitting H5827/H5829 help); Huram only H2438 Tyrian variant (omitting H2361 Benjaminite); Malcham person was offered only deity H4445; Caesarea Philippi is not the Macedonian Philippi.

Meaning disagreements are recorded as disputed, not proof that either historical dictionary is correct. Unflattering or anatomical senses are attributed lexical proposals, not judgments about biblical persons. Peresh H6570/H6569 explicitly supplies its differing sense; Jezebel remains unresolved rather than receiving an invented offensive replacement.

H3120 says Javan son of Joktan whereas Genesis 10:2 has Japheth; H7262 labels Rabshakeh Babylonian whereas 2 Kings 18:17 concerns Assyria; H2317 calls Hadrach a deity whereas Zechariah 9:1 speaks of its land. KJV identity wording takes precedence over dictionary commentary.

Misspellings/malformed KJV fields and anomalous root links in the digital snapshot require checking original print before correction is attributed to Strong himself. Examples: G107 Azorigin, H2605 Canan, H2518 Hillkiah, H3339 Isri, H4122 hash/bash variant, H4409 remnant despite reign derivation, G3160 G4992 comparison, H3169 H3388 link, H2059 H3461 link, H8053 H8103 link and H6355 pit versus ruler disagreement.
Preserve explicit KJV naming explanations/wordplay separately from dictionary root proposals; Strong's alternative wording does not override the scriptural narrative.
Strong's Solomon identifications, imaginary description, eschatological labels and brothel interpretation are commentary; they are not independently established by the name etymology.
Separate commands, inscription words, titles, book/music headings, group labels and personal names. Some inputs lack KJV occurrences for their exact spelling.

Read-only inspection of public/data/kjv_verses.json found the Psalm 22 Aijeleth Shahar heading appended to Psalms 21:13. This review does not change the governing text or source vault; title location must not be mistaken for that verse's canonical wording.

Unmatched entries retain their input names and evidence limits. An unmatched spelling is not proof that the biblical person/place or the historical headword does not exist. No unresolved input was silently dropped.

Shared English spellings can cover different people, places, peoples, Hebrew entries, common words or titles. The review preserves key distinctions explicitly; it does not assert a complete verse-by-verse prosopography for all bearers.

Meshach is the imposed name of Mishael and Shadrach of Hananiah in Daniel 1:7; their faithful conduct belongs to the Scriptural narrative, not to a guessed name meaning.

findings: Coverage: all 873 assigned input rows received individual semantic review; one output row per name, in input order. No canonical Scripture, PDF, dictionary, source-vault, UI or git changes were made by this reviewer.

Operational source limitation: every Strong attribution here means the pinned OpenScriptures digital transcription at revision 0acd2f251c2d35ff8db2dece4e0593979d3ac223, as recorded in audit/name-sources/sources.json. This review did not collate 873 entries against original printed-edition facsimiles. Snapshot inconsistencies are not proof that James Strong printed those errors.

Status semantics: corroborated means the proposed displayMeaning has substantive lexical support after contextual review, sometimes selecting only one of Hitchcock's alternatives. Notes explicitly identify unestablished alternatives. It does not certify the entire original Hitchcock gloss, prove an etymology, or turn a dictionary claim into biblical fact. Disputed records dictionary disagreement, not proof which dictionary is correct.

Hitchcock remains an attributed historical source. Repeated meadow-versus-mourning, reversed grammatical subject, uncertain foreign-name, and patronymic-versus-root-gloss patterns require bounded editorial treatment; they do not justify a blanket rejection of Hitchcock.

KJV identity checks against public/data/kjv_verses.json confirm: Genesis 10:22 places Arphaxad among Shem's children while snapshot H775 says son of Noah; 1 Chronicles 20:5 calls Lahmi brother of Goliath the Gittite while H3902 says Israelite; 1 Chronicles 8:32 has Mikloth begetting Shimeah while H4732 calls Mikloth a place. Do not propagate those snapshot descriptions.

Christian/scriptural boundary: H6005's type name of Isaiah's son and G623's Satan parenthesis are commentary, not lexical definitions or KJV wording. Matthew 1:23 explicitly gives God with us and applies Emmanuel to Jesus Christ. Candace in Acts 8:27 is queen of the Ethiopians, whereas G2582 calls an Egyptian queen. G3532's heretic label for Nicolas is not established by Acts 6:5.

Distinct forms/identities needing separate records or context: Ahihud H282/H284; Amos H5986 versus G301/H531; Hadad H1908 versus H2301; Hadar H1924/H2316; Haran H2039/H2771; Heber H2268 versus Eber H5677; Ishi H3469 versus husband H376; On H203/H204; Puah H6312/H6326; Rahab Egypt H7294 versus woman H7343; Sarah Abraham's wife H8283 versus Asher's daughter H8294; Shiloh epithet H7886 versus place H7887.

Word/title contamination: Abba, antichrist, Asuppim, bekah, Nazirite/Nazarite, phylacteries, Pur, Rabbi, Shibboleth, Shiggaion, Shoshannim, Talitha cumi, teraphim and tetrarch should not become ordinary personal-name nodes. Book and festival titles also need their own types. Ahasuerus, Agag, Christ, Magdalene, Rab-saris and Zelotes require designation/title-aware presentation.

Exact-candidate gaps are not source absence: H26 explicitly includes Abigail but its KJV field says Abigal; H1835 describes Dan but its KJV field says Daniel; H1403 says Garbriel; G3683 identifies Onesiphorus but prints Onespiphorus; H1996 prints Hamogog; H445 prints Elkanan for Elhanan; H6611 prints Pethakiah; H5318 prints Neptoah; H8137 prints Senazar. Clear aliases were reviewed individually; weak similarities remain uncertain/unmatched.

Digital cross-reference mismatches include G137 -> G5869 instead of the Hebrew H5869; G3156 Matthew -> G3164 fight; G745 Archelaus/G3532 Nicolas -> G2994 Laodiceus where people is intended; H3169 strengthened -> H3388 Jerusha; H3844 white mountain -> H3825 heart; H4558 number -> H4457 tongs; and H8060 destructive -> H8073 Shamlai. These need original-edition collation before attributing the apparent defects to Strong himself.

Offensive/negative proposals are preserved with attribution and limits: G954 dung-god is the snapshot's parody proposal, not an uncited replacement; Rahab's two Hebrew names remain distinct; animal-derived names and negative root glosses are not moral judgments about people. No testimony was rewritten to make a name fit a gloss.

Webster1828 limitation: this reviewer did not independently inspect Webster entries. English paraphrases are editorial clarity proposals; any claimed Webster definition or historical English equivalence requires the primary agent's Webster source review. No claim of completed Webster collation is made here.

Remaining unmatched exact labels: Hamoth, Jaazah, Matthal, Shamed, Zeror, Zimzi. Their rows and Hitchcock glosses are retained unresolved rather than assigned guessed Strong identifiers. Near-spelling candidates are explicitly qualified throughout.
